description:
FILED s536h (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) while writing the #4284 guard row.  PRE-EXISTING (base ba7863a3 identical).  LOW: mixing buffered and unbuffered reads on one handle is documented as unwise in perlfunc sysread.

    open(my $h, "<", $f);   # $f holds "a\nb\n"
    read($h, my $buf, 1); my $n = sysread($h, $buf, 1); print "$n\n";
  perl 5.40.3: 0 (PerlIO's first fill read all 4 bytes; read(2) on the fd is at EOF)      PCL: 1

PCL's sysread (%p-sysread-impl -> %p-read-impl with %p-read-available) reads the same SBCL fd-stream buffer the buffered read filled.  An exact model needs sysread to read the descriptor directly (sb-unix:unix-read on the fd) past the CL buffer, which then also makes a later buffered read return the CL buffer's bytes first -- perl's order.  Decide whether to model it (perlfunc: "mixing reads and sysreads ... can cause confusion") or register it in docs/not-supported.md.  Probe: the first draft of Pl/t/errno-magic-01.t row 9 (s536h) -- it used one handle for read and sysread.
subject: sysread after a BUFFERED read on the same handle reads PCL's shared CL buffer; perl's sysread reads the descriptor (bypasses PerlIO's buffer): `read($h,$b,1); sysread($h,$b,1)` on a 4-byte file is 0 in perl (the buffer took the rest), 1 in PCL
